body:
Part of #114; split out under the reopening comment's instruction to ship all requirements or create linked follow-ups. PR #116 adds actionable Full Disk Access errors for conventional Safari cookie stores and shared synthetic decoder fixtures.

Complete the remaining platform diagnostics, discovery and parity requirements:

- Locked profiles/stores: consistent read-only snapshots as attach snapshot does; meaningful lock errors and snapshot guidance, including Windows sharing violations and SQLite contention. Never increase timeouts to hide recurring lock failures.
- macOS Safari protection failures for all stores (not just cookies): EPERM/EACCES must name the app that needs Full Disk Access and provide x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_AllFiles. Browser-wide listings should preserve protected-source errors and still list readable sources.
- Chromium Safe Storage Keychain prompts: clear errors identifying the key/service requested and the supported retry path; no silent fallback from protected data.
- profile sources/cookies sources domain discovery for all implemented per-site stores, reporting only names and counts. Safari binarycookies contains plaintext values in the file; decode only host metadata for listing, never expose values.
- Shared source × target × data-class capability declarations, generated README matrix and CI validation in all three packages; distinguish same-engine full clones from translated imports and report actual unsupported capabilities.
- Native parity tests for options/reports and protection/locked-profile paths in JS/Python/Rust, plus fixture round trips into every target engine. Existing feature markers alone do not establish equivalent real-browser behavior.

Acceptance: Windows/macOS/Linux diagnostics tests where applicable, injected protection/lock tests, clean sources, CI-checked byte-identical shared capabilities and a precise README matrix. Keep #114 open until these and the linked source/target/data-class issues ship.
title: Complete import protection diagnostics and source-target-data parity matrix (#114)
